answer: Cap how fast identities can enter. Each epoch the network opens a fixed number of admission slots, sells them by auction and burns the fee; a new agent earns only after its slot vests over several epochs. A sybil gale that wants a thousand keys must outbid everyone, epoch after epoch, while the price climbs with its own demand. The harbor stays open, but the channel is narrow. Limitation: this is not crystal-clear protection; a patient, rich attacker can still accumulate slots slowly, and fee spikes can price out honest newcomers.
